subject: physical-education
title: Launch and diagnostic: movement screening without diagnosis
essential_question: How can understanding personal readiness and goal design help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about movement screening without diagnosis, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of movement screening without diagnosis.
Check, revise, or improve work about movement screening without diagnosis using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about movement screening without diagnosis.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “movement screening without diagnosis.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on movement screening without diagnosis. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.

Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about movement screening without diagnosis. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of movement screening without diagnosis and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about movement screening without diagnosis; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of movement screening without diagnosis and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about movement screening without diagnosis; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for movement screening without diagnosis, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for movement screening without diagnosis works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of movement screening without diagnosis, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking movement screening without diagnosis mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply movement screening without diagnosis under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting movement screening without diagnosis.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of movement screening without diagnosis in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

essential_question: How can understanding personal readiness and goal design help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for warm-up design, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of warm-up design.
Check, revise, or improve work about warm-up design using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about warm-up design.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “warm-up design.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on warm-up design. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about warm-up design. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of warm-up design and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about warm-up design; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of warm-up design and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about warm-up design; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for warm-up design, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for warm-up design works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of warm-up design, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking warm-up design mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply warm-up design under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting warm-up design.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of warm-up design in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

learning_objectives: Practice recovery and adaptation with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of recovery and adaptation.
Check, revise, or improve work about recovery and adaptation using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about recovery and adaptation.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “recovery and adaptation.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on recovery and adaptation. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about recovery and adaptation. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of recovery and adaptation and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about recovery and adaptation; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of recovery and adaptation and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about recovery and adaptation; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for recovery and adaptation, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for recovery and adaptation works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of recovery and adaptation, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking recovery and adaptation mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply recovery and adaptation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting recovery and adaptation.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of recovery and adaptation in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

learning_objectives: Practice fitness literacy with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of fitness literacy.
Check, revise, or improve work about fitness literacy using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about fitness literacy.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “fitness literacy.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on fitness literacy. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about fitness literacy. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of fitness literacy and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about fitness literacy; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of fitness literacy and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about fitness literacy; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for fitness literacy, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for fitness literacy works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of fitness literacy, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking fitness literacy mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply fitness literacy under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting fitness literacy.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of fitness literacy in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on leadership. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about leadership. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of leadership and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about leadership; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of leadership and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about leadership; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for leadership, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for leadership works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of leadership, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking leadership mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply leadership under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting leadership.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of leadership in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
